A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MOBODY and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing methods and experiments can be matched across the reorganization, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original MuJoCo and Adroit experiments, dynamics-prediction errors, component ablations, and hyperparameter results.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, rollout/BC-weight analyses, and target-data-size experiments.

M1.justification: The separate action encoders, shared state encoder and transition model, training losses, DARA regularization, and target-Q-weighted BC procedure remain unchanged. Reward-learning equations added to the main text already appeared in v2 Appendix B; alternative BC weights are experimental variants.

E1.justification: The documented experiments retain the four MuJoCo locomotion environments and Adroit Pen/Door with the same dynamics-shift coverage. Smaller target datasets change sample counts within existing tasks. Antmaze appears only in the new limitations discussion, without a described evaluation.

E2.justification: V3 adds SRPO and REAG to the comparisons in Tables 1, 4, and 5 alongside the five retained baselines. These materially strengthen the comparisons and sometimes outperform MOBODY. REAG's underlying work was previously cited as RADT, but v2 did not report its evaluation.

E3.justification: V3 introduces controls crossing rollout use with BC weighting and target-data budgets of 500, 1,000, and 2,000 transitions alongside 5,000. Section 4.3.2 also narrows the stated dynamics-MSE evaluation from four training checkpoints in v2 Section 4.4 to 1M steps, while Table 3 remains unchanged. The main benchmark settings and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: New Figure 4 separates the contributions of model rollouts and BC weighting. New Table 7 compares IQL-style and target-Q BC weights, while Table 8 examines sensitivity to target-data scarcity. These address mechanism attribution and data requirements beyond the retained component, dynamics-model, and hyperparameter ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three seeds for the principal comparisons and component ablations. Aggregate plots lack error bars in both; v3 explains this omission without changing the reporting practice. No new confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation table values are retained, but v3 adds substantial comparator and analysis results. For example, MOBODY's unchanged Adroit total of 333.10, which led v2's comparison, now trails REAG's reported 348.28. The new BC-weight and data-size tables add findings under additional conditions, rather than demonstrating improved same-setting MOBODY performance.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds SRPO's KL-constrained objective, its reward-shaping derivation and discriminator density-ratio expression, plus formal REAG return-augmentation definitions. MOBODY's existing mathematical formulation is retained, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and central methodological contributions remain essentially unchanged. The introduction reduces the reported gravity/friction advantage from approximately 58% to 44% following the stronger baseline comparison, and describes target-Q-weighted BC as empirically validated rather than emphasizing superiority over vanilla BC.

C2.justification: V3 newly attributes most gains to model rollouts and explains the auxiliary role of target-Q weighting. It adds explanations for DARA, BOSA, and SRPO behavior. New Appendix D explicitly discusses the shared-structure assumption, its possible breakdown under extreme shifts, and difficulties with sparse rewards.

D1.justification: V3 specifies seven ensemble transition models, further describes target-data collection, and documents SRPO's discriminator implementation and the evaluated REAG variant using CQL values. Hardware, timing results, existing hyperparameters, and the code-access URL are retained; the new reproducibility statement mostly consolidates existing information.

R1.justification: Appendix A substantially broadens positioning through a new discussion of robust MDP research without target data, including uncertainty-set requirements and conservatism. V3 also adds SRPO, decision-transformer, and reward-weighted-regression connections and expands distinctions from existing representation learning. The RADT/REAG publication update itself is not a new cited work.

P1.justification: Much of the abstract, introduction, and method prose is retained. V3 locally rewrites experimental discussion, incorporates former Section 4.4 into Section 4.3.2, subdivides the ablation material, separates computational analysis, and moves references before the appendices. Conference headers and additional disclosure statements also change.

P2.justification: V3 extensively reformats the document, places Tables 1–3 near their main-text discussions, and shrinks Figure 2 into a wrapped layout. It adds Figure 4 and Tables 7–8, expands comparator columns and legends, and consolidates the hyperparameter table. Redrawn Figure 5 also corrects the swapped gravity/friction panels in v2 Figure 4.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens an already substantial empirical study with stronger comparators, clearer component attribution, data-scarcity tests, explicit limitations, and corrected shift-plot labels. These benefits outweigh limited reporting problems, but some new summaries remain inconsistent: Table 1 supports 27 top-two finishes rather than the stated 28, and Tables 7–8 report 41.46 where retained Table 1 reports 41.60 for HalfCheetah gravity-2.0.
